court: Court of Appeals for the Fifth Circuit

issues.label: Jurisdiction and proper venue
issues.why: The court must confirm it has authority to review the final order and that the petition is properly before it.

issues.label: Exhaustion of issues
issues.why: The court must determine whether each argument was presented to the BIA and thus is reviewable.

issues.label: Timeliness of petition
issues.why: Judicial review typically requires a timely filed petition for review of the BIA decision.

issues.label: Finality of removal order
issues.why: The court must verify there is a final, reviewable order after BIA dismissal.

issues.label: Scope of review
issues.why: The court must identify what portions of the IJ decision are incorporated into or relied on by the BIA.

issues.label: Standard of review
issues.why: The court must apply the correct standards (substantial evidence for facts/credibility; de novo for law).

issues.label: Removability determination
issues.why: The court must ensure the removability ground under 8 U.S.C. § 1182(a)(7)(A)(i) was properly established.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must ensure the IJ placed burdens correctly for removability and for each form of relief.

issues.label: Right to counsel advisals
issues.why: Because Eqbal was pro se, the IJ must have provided required advisals about counsel and available resources.

issues.label: Fair hearing and due process
issues.why: The court must assess whether pro se proceedings were fundamentally fair and the IJ adequately developed the record.

issues.label: Interpreter adequacy
issues.why: If language issues existed, accurate interpretation is required for meaningful participation and credibility assessment.

issues.label: Notice of charges and procedures
issues.why: Proper notice of the allegations, charges, and hearing procedures is required for due process.

issues.label: Opportunity to present evidence
issues.why: The IJ must have allowed Eqbal to testify, submit documents, and call witnesses as reasonably available.

issues.label: Opportunity to explain inconsistencies
issues.why: Due process and credibility rules require giving the respondent a chance to explain perceived discrepancies.

issues.label: Consideration of trauma effects
issues.why: The IJ should account for torture/trauma and time gaps when weighing memory-based inconsistencies.

issues.label: Adverse credibility legal framework
issues.why: The court must confirm the IJ applied the REAL ID Act credibility factors correctly and holistically.

issues.label: Materiality of inconsistencies
issues.why: The court must assess whether discrepancies about job titles/dates reasonably support an adverse credibility finding.

issues.label: Speculation and conjecture limits
issues.why: Credibility findings cannot rest on speculation about Afghan government roles or implausibility without record support.

issues.label: Demeanor findings adequacy
issues.why: If demeanor was cited, the IJ must provide specific, cogent reasons linked to the record.

issues.label: Consistency with country conditions
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether the IJ compared testimony with objective country evidence appropriately.

issues.label: Corroboration rule compliance
issues.why: The IJ must follow the required steps for demanding corroboration (identify, assess availability, allow explanation).

issues.label: Notice of corroboration needs
issues.why: The respondent must have meaningful notice of what specific corroborating evidence was expected.

issues.label: Reasonableness of evidence demands
issues.why: The IJ must assess whether requested corroboration was reasonably obtainable given flight, hiding, and Taliban control.

issues.label: Weight to non-testimonial evidence
issues.why: The IJ must not discount documents solely because testimony was found not credible without reasoned analysis.

issues.label: Authentication expectations
issues.why: The IJ must apply realistic standards for authenticating Afghan documents in asylum proceedings.

issues.label: Country reports consideration
issues.why: The IJ/BIA must meaningfully consider relevant reports about Taliban targeting former officials and Tajiks.

issues.label: Asylum one-year deadline
issues.why: The court must address whether the asylum application was timely or qualifies for exceptions based on entry date.

issues.label: Changed/extraordinary exceptions
issues.why: If timing is contested, the court must evaluate exceptions such as changed conditions or other extraordinary circumstances.

issues.label: Asylum eligibility elements
issues.why: The court must determine whether Eqbal showed past persecution or a well-founded fear on a protected ground.

issues.label: Protected ground identification
issues.why: The court must analyze claimed grounds: political opinion (actual/imputed), ethnicity (Tajik), and possibly PSG.

issues.label: Imputed political opinion
issues.why: Taliban targeting for prior government security work may constitute imputed anti-Taliban political opinion.

issues.label: Ethnicity nexus
issues.why: The court must assess whether harm is motivated at least in part by Tajik ethnicity.

issues.label: Particular social group viability
issues.why: If asserted or implicit, the court must analyze PSG cognizability (e.g., former Afghan government security personnel).

issues.label: Nexus standard for asylum
issues.why: The court must apply the ‘one central reason’ test for asylum motive.

issues.label: Nexus standard for withholding
issues.why: The court must apply the ‘a reason’ test and higher likelihood standard for withholding.

issues.label: Past persecution determination
issues.why: The 1997/1998 month-long torture and imprisonment must be evaluated as potential past persecution.

issues.label: Severity and cumulative harm
issues.why: The court must consider beatings, torture, lasting injury, threats, and family targeting cumulatively.

issues.label: Perpetrator as government actor
issues.why: Taliban actions then/now may constitute persecution by a governing authority, affecting presumptions and relocation.

issues.label: Presumption from past persecution
issues.why: If past persecution is found, a presumption of future persecution arises and DHS bears rebuttal burdens.

issues.label: Rebuttal: fundamental change
issues.why: The court must assess whether conditions changed such that future persecution is no longer likely (likely the opposite here).

issues.label: Rebuttal: internal relocation
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether safe, reasonable internal relocation within Afghanistan is possible under Taliban rule.

issues.label: Reasonableness of relocation
issues.why: Even if possible, relocation must be reasonable considering family, resources, and Taliban nationwide reach.

issues.label: Well-founded fear objective prong
issues.why: The court must assess objective reasonableness using warrants, active searching, colleague killings, and country evidence.

issues.label: Subjective fear
issues.why: The court must determine whether Eqbal genuinely fears return based on credible testimony and circumstances.

issues.label: Future persecution individualized risk
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether Eqbal is specifically targeted (warrants, searches, airport stop) beyond general violence.

issues.label: Family persecution relevance
issues.why: Assault and interrogation of his mother and ongoing inquiries can corroborate targeting and future risk.

issues.label: Pattern-or-practice claim
issues.why: The court must consider whether there is a pattern or practice of persecuting former government personnel or Tajiks.

issues.label: Government unable/unwilling
issues.why: For persecution analysis, the court must determine whether any Afghan authority could protect him (likely not under Taliban).

issues.label: Discretionary asylum factors
issues.why: If eligible, asylum requires favorable exercise of discretion and assessment of any adverse equities.

issues.label: Statutory bars to asylum
issues.why: The court must check for persecutor, serious nonpolitical crime, terrorism, firm resettlement, or security-related bars.

issues.label: Persecutor bar inquiry
issues.why: His security roles require assessing whether he assisted in persecution of others.

issues.label: Serious crime bar inquiry
issues.why: The record must be examined for any conviction or conduct triggering mandatory bars.

issues.label: Terrorism-related bars
issues.why: Any alleged association with armed groups or material support must be evaluated if raised by DHS or record evidence.

issues.label: Firm resettlement bar
issues.why: If he lived in another country before the U.S., the court must consider firm resettlement (not stated but must be checked).

issues.label: Withholding mandatory nature
issues.why: If the higher standard is met and no bars apply, withholding must be granted regardless of discretion.

issues.label: Withholding statutory bars
issues.why: The court must evaluate particularly serious crime, serious nonpolitical crime, and security-related withholding bars.

issues.label: CAT legal standard
issues.why: The court must apply the ‘more likely than not’ torture standard, independent of asylum nexus.

issues.label: Definition of torture
issues.why: The court must determine whether feared harm rises to severe pain/suffering intentionally inflicted for a purpose.

issues.label: CAT state action requirement
issues.why: Torture must be inflicted by or with consent/acquiescence of a public official or person acting in official capacity.

issues.label: Taliban as officials
issues.why: Because Taliban governs Afghanistan, their actions may satisfy CAT official-capacity requirements.

issues.label: Acquiescence and willful blindness
issues.why: If harm is by non-state actors, the court must analyze whether officials would acquiesce, including willful blindness.

issues.label: CAT evidence aggregation
issues.why: All risk factors must be considered cumulatively, including past torture, warrants, and country conditions.

issues.label: Past torture weight
issues.why: Prior torture is highly probative of future torture risk and must be meaningfully weighed.

issues.label: Internal relocation under CAT
issues.why: The court must consider whether Eqbal could avoid torture by relocating, and whether that is feasible.

issues.label: CAT protection type
issues.why: If CAT is granted, the court must determine whether withholding or deferral is appropriate given any bars.

issues.label: Reasoned explanation requirement
issues.why: The agency must provide a rational explanation connecting record evidence to findings on credibility and relief.

issues.label: BIA review adequacy
issues.why: The court must assess whether the BIA properly reviewed the IJ’s findings and addressed key arguments.

issues.label: Harmless error analysis
issues.why: If procedural or legal errors occurred, the court must decide whether they were prejudicial to the outcome.

issues.label: Record completeness
issues.why: The court must ensure the administrative record contains all relied-upon evidence and transcripts for review.

issues.label: Changed country conditions evidence
issues.why: The Taliban takeover and post-2021 targeting must be evaluated as central to future-risk analysis.

issues.label: Continuing interest evidence
issues.why: Warrants, searches, airport encounter, and continued family inquiries must be assessed for ongoing threat.

issues.label: Credibility vs burden on CAT
issues.why: Even with adverse credibility, CAT may be proven via independent evidence; the agency must separately analyze it.

issues.label: Documentary evidence independence
issues.why: The court must consider whether documents/country reports independently establish eligibility notwithstanding credibility findings.

issues.label: Pro se corroboration obstacles
issues.why: The court must consider whether detention and lack of counsel affected ability to obtain corroboration and present case.

issues.label: Mental/physical impairment relevance
issues.why: Back injury and health issues may affect testimony and ability to gather evidence and should be considered.

issues.label: Remedy on error
issues.why: If errors are found, the court must determine whether to remand for further proceedings or grant relief outright.
